To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a new algorithm that can be used to solve the power and admission control (PAC) problem for a wireless system.

(i) we reformulated the problem as a sparse optimization problem, and then relaxed it to a linear programming problem; (ii) we proposed a linear programming deflation algorithm to iteratively remove the strong interferers and solve the relaxed problem; (iii) we derived two easy-to-check conditions to determine the strong interferers; and (iv) we proposed a heuristic to improve the performance of our algorithm.
we propose a new method for solving the power and admission control (PAC) problem in a wireless network that is more accurate than the existing ones and has lower computational complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the joint admission control and power allocation problem for wireless networks.
the joint power and access control problem in a wireless network.
the joint power and interference control problem in a multiuser wireless network.

the proposed approach is a good alternative to existing approaches in terms the number of supported users, the total transmission, and the execution complexity.
the proposed algorithm is a promising approach for the joint power and interference control problem in wireless networks, especially when the network size is relatively large.
our proposed method is the best in all aspects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a simple and efficient solution for the joint power and interference control problem in wireless networks.

we provide a simple, yet effective, approach for solving the joint power and link admission control problem for wireless networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple linear program relaxation of a sparse l0- minimization problem is a very effective tool for joint power and admission in wireless networks, and that it can be further enhanced by a deflation procedure that iteratively removes strong interfering links.
the joint power and access control problem can be solved efficiently by using the linear programming (LP) deflation approach.
deflation is a powerful tool for solving NP-hard joint power and admission problems in wireless networks.
